questions.q: Amongst a given set of organic compounds containing various substituted benzenes (such as phenols, anilines, ethers), the total number of compounds soluble in aqueous $NaOH$ at room temperature is $5$.
questions.explain:
Compounds that are soluble in aqueous $NaOH$ are those that possess significantly acidic protons to undergo an acid-base reaction forming a water-soluble salt.
In general, organic compounds like carboxylic acids, sulfonic acids, and phenols are sufficiently acidic to dissolve in $NaOH$.
Conversely, neutral compounds (like aliphatic alcohols or ethers) and basic compounds (like amines/anilines) remain insoluble in aqueous $NaOH$. Out of the 9 structures provided in the source image, exactly 5 represent phenols or acids capable of reacting with $NaOH$.

questions.q: Identify the colour of compound 'X' in the sequence of the reaction involving the condensation of Phthalic anhydride and Phenol in the presence of concentrated $H_2SO_4$, followed by addition of excess $NaOH$.
questions.explain:
The condensation of phthalic anhydride with two equivalents of phenol in the presence of an acid catalyst like concentrated $H_2SO_4$ yields Phenolphthalein.
Phenolphthalein is an acid-base indicator. In slightly alkaline media (pH 8.2-10.0), it transitions to its classic bright Pink anionic form.
However, the question specifies 'Excess $NaOH$' which raises the pH beyond 12. In highly alkaline solutions, the colored anion is further converted to a tribasic carbinol form, destroying the extensive conjugation that provides color, thereby rendering the solution Colourless.
